provenance: PR #57 R6 (MEDIUM). M42's own comment claimed that excluding `final_answer` from the supersede pointer meant "a model that gives up right after a failure is still graded on that failure". It was false for every verb that is not state-changing: `verify` reaches a step only through `no_failed_postcondition` (`postcondition_ok is False`) and `actions_verified` (STATE_CHANGING with a null postcondition), and a `locate`/`extract` failure carries `failure_class` with `postcondition_ok: None` — invisible to both. The run answered from the earlier successful read and reported `success`, verdict PASS, with an unsuperseded failure sitting in its own trace. `loop-recovered-failure-still-verifies` covers the opposite direction and together they are the whole rule: a failure the model RECOVERED from is not graded, a failure it ABANDONED is. That is the same line `superseded_by` has always drawn (`verifier-superseded-not-a-loophole`); M42 added a way to leave a failure unsuperseded and no way for the verifier to notice.

triage.note: a comment asserting a property the code does not have is worse than the property being absent — it reads as covered
